prompt: Match each audience to the unit it thinks in.
Which of the four audiences is most important, by the lesson?
hint: The analysis has to pass through them.

choices.text: The board, because it sets the targets for everyone else
choices.why: It can set a target and still fail to get the change made.

choices.text: Management
choices.why: It can approve a pilot a distrustful technical team undermines.

choices.text: None of them
choices.why: The analysis usually has to pass through all four, and each can stop it.

choices.text: The client
choices.why: Most important only when the client is the one paying you.

prompt: Before the meeting you learn the group will decide nothing. What does the lesson suggest?
hint: The first of the three questions.

choices.text: Present anyway, with fewer slides
choices.why: Fewer slides do not create a decision.

choices.text: Ask them for a decision they do not own
choices.why: That puts a request in front of a room that cannot grant it.

choices.text: It is information, and probably an email
choices.why: A presentation earns its slot by asking for something.

choices.text: Cancel the analysis because nobody will act on it in the near future
choices.why: The analysis is fine; the format is wrong for this room.

prompt: What makes a board stop listening, by the lesson?

choices.text: A table
choices.why: Tables ask the board to analyse; it wants the finding in its unit.

choices.text: An undefined term in the method section
choices.why: That loses the technical team.

choices.text: A hint that the carrier is being blamed for the delays
choices.why: That loses the client.

choices.text: A number in reais
choices.why: That is exactly what it wants.

prompt: What decision does Marina ask the board for?

choices.text: To approve the eight-week pilot
choices.why: Management approves pilots; asking the board bypasses Paulo.

choices.text: To replace Ligeiro with another carrier for every first order
choices.why: The cause is in Faro's warehouse, not the carrier.

choices.text: To fund a new logistics team
choices.why: The fix needs no new spending.

choices.text: To track the first-delivery on-time rate every quarter
choices.why: Cheap, at board level, and it makes the problem somebody's job after the pilot is forgotten.

prompt: How many customers a year does the lesson say cancel early who would not have if their first box had been on time?
hint: Lesson 11 shows where it comes from.

prompt: Why should the technical team and finance check the numbers before the board sees them?

choices.text: The board trusts the numbers as far as it trusts who checked them
choices.why: It will not see the method, so the checking has to have happened already.

choices.text: Board members are not able to read charts
choices.why: Nothing in the lesson says so.

choices.text: It is a legal requirement
choices.why: The reason given is trust, not law.

choices.text: To delay the presentation
choices.why: The sequence speeds it up.

prompt: Why should Marina not open Paulo's version with the R$ 790 thousand?
hint: Paulo already knows cancellations cost money.

choices.text: The number is wrong
choices.why: It is the same number in every version.

choices.text: It reads as going over his head
choices.why: Management leads with the choice in front of it; the money framing is the board's.

choices.text: Money is confidential inside Faro
choices.why: Confidentiality is the client section's concern, not Paulo's.

choices.text: Managers prefer percentages to amounts in reais when they compare options
choices.why: Not the lesson's reason.

prompt: What does Paulo's opening sentence contain? Choose all that apply.
hint: The inverted pyramid, with management's content.

choices.text: The lever
choices.why: Remove one step from first orders.

choices.text: The expected effect
choices.why: From 17.3% toward 8%.

choices.text: The owner and the start date
choices.why: Sandra's team, 1 September.

choices.text: The method of the analysis
choices.why: One sentence later, at most.

prompt: What question sits behind every question Paulo asks?
hint: Answer it in the risks slide.

choices.text: Is the analysis statistically sound?
choices.why: That is Diego's question.

choices.text: How much does the board care?
choices.why: He may wonder, but the lesson names another.

choices.text: Who did the analysis, and how long has she been here?
choices.why: Trust matters, but it is not the question behind his.

choices.text: What happens to my people and targets?
choices.why: Answering it in advance is what lets a manager decide in the room.

prompt: Which risk of the pilot does the lesson say to state plainly?
hint: Something the check was there to catch.

choices.text: Some boxes may go to a mistyped address
choices.why: How many is unknown, and the pilot measures it.

choices.text: Ligeiro may cancel the contract
choices.why: Nothing suggests that; Ligeiro is asked for two small favours.

choices.text: The board may reject the quarterly measure
choices.why: That is a board matter, not a risk of the pilot.

choices.text: Customers may notice the change
choices.why: If they do, it is a box arriving on time.

prompt: Why does the technical version open with definitions?

choices.text: Technical audiences like tables
choices.why: Taste is not the reason.

choices.text: To slow the discussion down
choices.why: It speeds it up.

choices.text: Because a dispute about the conclusion becomes a check of one definition
choices.why: Diego's on-time rate might use a different promised date; settling that first is a short conversation.

choices.text: Definitions are required by law in reports
choices.why: No such law is mentioned.

prompt: If Diego can rebuild 41.5% himself, he stops being a reviewer and becomes a ___.
The exit survey puts price first and delivery third. What does the lesson say to do with that in the technical review?

choices.text: Leave it out, since it weakens the case
choices.why: A caveat the reviewer finds himself costs more trust than one you showed.

choices.text: Show it
choices.why: This audience gets every level, including what weakens the case; lesson 12 explains why it does not undo the finding.

choices.text: Change the finding to price
choices.why: Only 23% answered the survey; behaviour says something different.

choices.text: Ask Diego to run a new survey before the review
choices.why: That postpones the review without answering anything.

prompt: Why does the technical review usually come before the management meeting?

choices.text: So the finding arrives with Sandra's analyst behind it
choices.why: "Did you talk to my team?" already has an answer.

choices.text: Because technical people have more time
choices.why: Time is not the reason.

choices.text: Management refuses to see unchecked numbers
choices.why: Not a rule at Faro; the benefit is the ally, not a gate.

choices.text: So the analyst can practise the talk on a friendlier audience before the real one
choices.why: A technical review is not friendly practice; it is the hardest check.

prompt: Why does Marina not show Ligeiro the R$ 790 thousand?

choices.text: It is not accurate enough for an external audience
choices.why: Accuracy is not the issue.

choices.text: It tells a supplier its leverage in the next negotiation
choices.why: Share what the client needs to act, and nothing more.

choices.text: Ligeiro would not understand it
choices.why: Understanding is not the problem.

choices.text: Money must never be shown in slides
choices.why: The board version leads with it.

prompt: The analysis found the delay is mostly caused inside Faro's warehouse. How should that shape the talk with Ligeiro?

choices.text: Keep it quiet so Ligeiro does more
choices.why: Implying their fault would be false and would poison the conversation.

choices.text: Say it plainly, framed as a shared goal in the contract's terms
choices.why: Good news for the relationship, and the honest framing.

choices.text: Do not present to Ligeiro at all
choices.why: Two small requests make the pilot work and measurable.

choices.text: Present the full internal deck
choices.why: That shares commercially sensitive numbers.

prompt: What does Faro ask of Ligeiro? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Collect first orders in the afternoon pickup
choices.why: Small, and it speeds the first box.

choices.text: Send delivered scans daily
choices.why: So the pilot can be measured as it runs.

choices.text: Lower its prices
choices.why: Not part of this request, and it would sour it.

choices.text: Take over the address check
choices.why: The step is being removed, not moved.

prompt: You work for a consultancy and the client is the company that hired you. What changes, by the lesson?

choices.text: Nothing
choices.why: The client's own rooms are added.

choices.text: You stop framing problems as things to fix
choices.why: That still applies.

choices.text: Its board, management and technical team are three more rooms
choices.why: And the first three sections of the lesson apply to each.

choices.text: You share everything, since they paid for the analysis
choices.why: Share what serves their decision.

prompt: Put the four rooms in the order of how much depth each gets, from most to least.
hint: Every level, two, the part that concerns them, one.
trap: The client gets only its part, which can be deep in one place; the board gets one level everywhere.
